motivatingPathology: Manual breaks force layout: a hard page break ending one paragraph and a column break ending the next, each as a typed break element inside its own run. Typed breaks paginate without adding paragraphs, so converting a page break into a paragraph mark changes the document structure. The engine must carry both break types through ingest, mutation of nearby sentences, and rezip without converting breaks to paragraphs or swapping their types.
knownLimitations: Two break types appear once each; text-wrapping breaks with clear attributes live in the sibling fixture. One paragraph per break type is the whole shape; consecutive breaks are not exercised. Last-rendered page breaks and multi-column interaction are not covered. Breaks inside table cells are absent. Rendered pagination is never asserted.
scopeExclusions: This fixture does not exercise line breaks, hyphenation controls, tab characters, or symbol characters; those live in sibling fixtures. Section breaks that change page geometry are covered by the section-layout fixtures, not here. Rendered page and column breaks are never measured; only markup preservation and schema validity are.
ecma376Difficulty: Breaks are typed empty elements whose type attribute decides geometry: page, column, or text-wrapping with clearing. A writer that drops the type keeps a break that does the wrong thing, and one that expands breaks into empty paragraphs changes node counts. The type attribute must round-trip exactly or pagination silently changes.
licenseProvenance: Hand-built for this corpus from the ECMA-376 transitional schema; no third-party source material; fixture bytes under the repository license.

disposition.reason: Typed page and column breaks are Word-legal and safe, so the engine preserves both types: the paragraph node checksums are identical after the round trip and the package validates clean.
